sections.h2: Where do White County taxpayers go to pay?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's lobby is at 506 North Main Street in Cleveland, and the mailing address is P. O. Box 970, Cleveland, GA 30528. Call 706-865-2225. The drive-thru lane opens at 8 am and shuts at 4:30 pm, while the lobby stays open until 4:50 pm, Monday through Friday.

Bills go out each August with a November 15 deadline. You can pay with cash, check or card at the counter, or online, and the county notes that convenience fees apply to cards and web payments. The same office bills timber, real and personal property, mobile homes, utilities and motor vehicles, and it registers vehicles for the state.

Values are a different counter. The assessors work out of Suite 180 in the Mauney Building, and their board sits on the second Wednesday of each month at 9 a.m. to talk through appeals, homestead requests and changes in taxation status.

sections.h2: Why do White County homes cost more than their neighbors'?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page puts the median owner-occupied home at $278,900 for 2020 through 2024. The county covers 240.74 square miles and had 29,802 people in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.4% from April 2020. Cleveland, Helen and Sautee Nacoochee are the communities the county site names.

Nature and travel feed that demand. The county's recreation list includes Anna Ruby Falls, Dukes Creek Falls, Hardman Farm State Historic Site, Smithgall Woods State Park and Unicoi State Park and Lodge, and its schools belong to the White County School System.

  • Owner-occupied share: 78.8% of 14,547 housing units.
  • Median rent: $1,032. Construction permits in 2025: 190.
  • Residents 65 and older: 25.4%. Median household income: $70,666.
  • Average drive to work: 30.4 minutes, and 10,729 households average 2.63 people.

On the business side, QuickFacts shows 733 employer businesses and 7,240 jobs in 2023, with a payroll of $286.1 million, 2022 retail sales of $520.5 million and $132.8 million spent in lodging and restaurants. The county also counts 1,862 veterans, and its poverty rate is 10.8%. Among adults 25 and older, 84.8% finished high school and 24.0% hold a bachelor's degree.

sections.h2: How does White County turn a value into a tax bill?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is assessed value, minus exemptions, times the millage rate. Georgia assesses at 40% of fair market value unless a rule says otherwise, and each mill means one dollar for every $1,000 of assessed value. The assessors set the value, and the taxing bodies set the rate.

The county commissioners and the Board of Education are the main rate setters. A notice on the county home page for 2026 shows the commissioners planning to cut the county millage rate to 8.555 mills from the 8.842 mills of 2025, a drop of 0.287 mills. That is the county government's piece only, so school and city levies stack on top. Cleveland and Helen are separate cities, so ask the commissioner whether a city levy touches your address.

Owners file a return of real property from January 1 to April 1, and a missing return means the prior year's value stands. The assessors then mail an Annual Notice of Assessment listing last year's value, this year's value, an estimate at last year's millage and the reason for any change. You can look up your record by name or address on the county's property records site, which is also where the homestead application opens.

sections.h2: What is the White County window for contesting a value?
sections.html:
The window lasts 45 days from the date printed on the Annual Notice of Assessment, which usually goes out in early May. Six grounds qualify: value, uniformity, taxability, denial of exemption, breach of covenant and denial of covenant. The bill itself is not appealable in Georgia.

Nobody can extend the deadline. The county says a missed window waives the appeal for that year and the Board of Assessors has no power to make an exception. If you agree with the notice, you do nothing.

Appeals that reach the Board of Equalization go before what the county calls a special jury for property values and denied exemptions. Questions about it go to the Clerk of Court at 706-865-2613.

sections.h2: How do I claim a homestead exemption in White County?
sections.html:
Use the online application inside the property records site and finish it by April 1 for the current year. The house must be your primary residence, with no homestead claimed elsewhere in Georgia or another state, and a Georgia driver's license or ID showing the street address is required. A late application rolls forward to the following year.

The county says it offers numerous homestead exemptions and sends owners to the assessor for the list. Two other programs share the page. Freeport exemption covers business inventory, and a voter-approved local percentage of 20, 40, 60, 80 or 100 applies; the county notes that over sixty percent of Georgia counties and cities have adopted it at some level. Conservation use assessment covers up to 2,000 acres of farm or timber land under Georgia Code 48-5-7.4, for a single owner who signs a ten-year covenant. Freeport applications go to the Board of Assessors in the same period returns are due, and later ones can earn a partial exemption until June 1.

sections.h2: What happens when White County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
After November 15 a balance picks up penalties and moves toward liens, levies and finally a tax sale. The commissioner still accepts payment on a delinquent bill, though interest keeps running. A lien, also called a Fi. Fa., sits on record with the Clerk of Court for seven years and may hurt credit reports and ratings.

A levy seizes part of the property to cover the debt, and personal property may be taken, counted and stored. The county says a sign may go up, extra fees are added, and the owner can stay in the house. A tax sale gets four consecutive weeks of advertising in the White County News and happens on the first Tuesday of a month at the courthouse steps. The sale adds its own advertising and conduct fees. Buyers pay in certified funds and receive a Sheriff's tax deed, issued with a receipt from the commissioner.

The original owner has a year to redeem, and lien and mortgage holders may redeem as well. After that the buyer may foreclose the right of redemption. The county says a lien is removed by paying the delinquent balance with fees and interest, so a seller should request that payoff from the commissioner and hand it to the closing attorney.

faqs.q: What is the due date for White County property tax?
faqs.a: November 15. Bills are sent every August. After that date penalties begin, and interest keeps accruing on a delinquent bill.

faqs.q: Where is the White County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: 506 North Main Street, Cleveland, with the phone at 706-865-2225. The lobby closes at 4:50 pm and the drive-thru at 4:30 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: When must a White County value dispute be filed?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, usually mailed in early May. The Board of Assessors cannot extend that deadline.

faqs.q: By what date does a White County homestead application have to arrive?
faqs.a: April 1, to count for the current year. Applications are accepted all year, but a late one shifts the benefit forward. The home must be your primary residence.

faqs.q: Will a White County tax lien block a house sale?
faqs.a: The county says a lien comes off when the delinquent balance, fees and interest are paid. Ask the commissioner for that payoff figure and give it to the closing attorney.
